more_info.banned_in:
Banned in: United States.
Approved in the EU.
FDA cancelled food-use certificates for FD&C Red No. 2 in 1976.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
The EU rules checked in 2026 prohibit sale of this colour directly to consumers; specified uses in manufactured foods remain separately authorised.
more_info.overview: Amaranth is a synthetic red azo colour, also known as FD&C Red No. 2. It supplies red shades in foods where its use is permitted. The dye is chemically identified under C.I. Food Red 9. The specified colour is supplied as a reddish-brown powder or granules.
more_info.origin: Synthetic. Naphthalenesulfonic acid compounds are coupled to form the dye, which is supplied mainly as the sodium salt.
more_info.daily_intake: 0.15 mg/kg body weight per day (EFSA, 2010). JECFA allocated 0–0.5 mg/kg body weight per day in 1984; the values differ.
more_info.side_effects:
At estimated food-use exposure, EFSA's 2013 refined assessment placed all assessed age groups below its ADI. This estimates intake and does not establish that no individual reactions occur.
Long-term and reproductive/developmental animal studies were used to derive EFSA's lower ADI in 2010; these are experimental hazard data rather than demonstrated effects at ordinary human food intakes.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain fish roe; spirit drinks as defined in Regulation 2019/787.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
